transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start: 09:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Torres (Helix SRE), Leo Chen (ML Engineer), Priya Rao (Eng Manager)

Summary: Quick recap of last week's ttft improvements; looked at variance spikes; agreed to run microbench variants.

---
[00:00:08] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick agenda — perf recap, seqlen distribution, kernel tradeoffs, and next steps. Samir, do you want to kick off with the numbers you pulled?
[00:00:22] Samir: yeah sure, um, i pulled the 48-hour run from the pilot cluster — we saw median TTFT drop about 12% when we enabled the early token fastpath from last week, but the P95 didn't budge much, still some microburst tail. we also tried the s4-like matmul kernel on a subset, which improved microburst variance but increased steady-state token cost ~4%.
[00:00:45] Leo: real quick, when you say early token fastpath, is that the streaming handshake change or the prefix cache? i think our workload is heavy on short completions so the handshake matters.
[00:00:58] Samir: good question, it's both — the handshake reduces RTT on initial bytes, and the prefix/KV cache avoids recomputing embeddings for repeated prefixes. for your short completions the handshake was the biggest win, but the KV cash warmup still shows in bursts — sorry, "KV cash" — kv cache — yeah.
[00:01:12] Ava: small note, our traffic has a lot of bursts at 30s intervals we couldn't flatten — i uploaded a sample trace to the shared folder, it should show the bursts around 03:00 UTC.
[00:01:26] Samir: got it, that trace helped. when we overlayed it with the matmul kernel run there was fewer extreme tails but more consistent median which is why cost went up a little.
[00:01:40] Priya: can you translate cost into our units? like per-100k requests? we need that to decide whether to accept the 4% uplift.
[00:01:50] Maya: yes we'll put a quick calc in the one-pager Samir and i will send — we can show two levers: keep default kernel + aggressive batching for cost, or s4-like kernel + lower batching for latency.
[00:02:05] Samir: also worth flagging sequence length distribution. your P90 is ~78 tokens, but mean is 42. so if we optimize for P95 the config changes a bit: kernel selection and batch timeout must be different versus optimizing for median.
[00:02:25] Leo: our user flows vary — some are very short (20-30 tokens) but a subset of assisted writing hits 200+ occasionally. is hedging by route possible?
[00:02:38] Samir: yes, smart routing by workload class is exactly where Redwood routing policies shine — you can route short completions to a low-latency, higher-cost pool and long sequences to cheaper, batched pools. we demo'd a policy like that in the onboarding deck.
[00:02:52] Priya: fine, but operationally that's more complexity. for the POC we wanted minimal ops work. what's the simplest change that gives us the biggest TTFT win?
[00:03:02] Samir: handshake + lowering batcher timeout from 20ms to 5-10ms for the short-pool gives most wins for short completions. does add cost but minimal infra changes.
[00:03:15] Ava: what's the risk to stability if we lower timeouts? we've seen occasional OOM-ish failures during big microbursts.
[00:03:24] Samir: lowering timeouts trades off throughput so peak GPU memory pressure might go up; but we can limit concurrency per model instance and enable autoscale thresholds. we'll include suggested concurrency caps in the config diff.
[00:03:38] Maya: also we can enable prefix caching aggressively for flows that repeat prompts — that reduces compute at the cost of cache memory.
[00:03:48] Leo: couple of uh, practical asks — can you run microbenches with seqlen 64 and 128 and the s4-like kernel so we can see the delta? and include the streaming handshake trace please.
[00:04:00] Samir: yep that's the plan. i'll run three variants: default kernel, s4-like kernel, and s4-like with smaller batch timeout. i'll include the handshake tracer and kv cache warmup times.
[00:04:13] Priya: what about the canary? we want to try on Dedicated for a short low-traffic window but need security signoff.
[00:04:21] Maya: we can schedule a 2-hour canary next Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC — that's low traffic per the traces Ava shared. Priya, can you confirm SSO/roles so Redwood can create the canary access?
[00:04:34] Priya: yes i'll ask security to whitelist the service principal, but we need the security notes first.
[00:04:40] Maya: i'll send a short note on SSO and the minimum audit logs we need, and a checklist.
[00:04:46] Ava: also side question — we talked about model quantization last month, did that land anywhere?
[00:04:52] Samir: we tried int8 quant on the dev branch, perf was mixed for your model due to attention path sensitivity; it reduced token cost but increased some latency variance — not recommended for short completions right now.
[00:05:06] Leo: ok good to know.
[00:05:09] Maya: quick recap before we close: Samir to run microbench variants, Ava to share full RPS trace and microburst hour, Maya to send config diff and security notes. reconvene same time next week to review results and decide canary.
[00:05:23] Priya: timeline works. anything else?
[00:05:27] Ava: one more, can you include a simple cost sensitivity table? e.g., latency delta vs per-100k request cost change.
[00:05:34] Maya: yes that's in the one-pager.
[00:05:38] Samir: i'll also include a small script to reproduce the microbench locally if you want to run it in your infra.
[00:05:45] Leo: thanks all.
[00:05:47] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts in the shared drive.
---
